title: Cuthbert and the otters
hookLine: after praying all night in the sea, Cuthbert is warmed by otters

lines: A MONK SLIPS OUT AT NIGHT.
INTO THE SEA, UP TO HIS NECK.
cards: Somebody is following him. It's the middle of the night at a monastery by the sea, and a guest, a monk named Cuthbert, has slipped out while everyone sleeps. He does this, apparently.
One of the brothers has noticed, and tonight curiosity wins. He creeps after him, keeping his distance, down toward the shore, expecting, maybe, to catch the holy man doing something ordinary.
Instead he watches Cuthbert walk straight into the sea, deeper and deeper, until the cold water is up around his neck. And there he stays.

teach.b: The story comes from Bede, who wrote a life of Cuthbert. Cuthbert stands in the sea through the dark hours, Bede says, singing praises to God with the waves. At dawn he wades out and kneels on the sand to pray.
Then two small animals come up out of the sea after him.

They stretch out in front of him, warm his feet with their breath, and dry them with their fur. Cuthbert blesses them, and they slip back into the water. The story is known today as Cuthbert and the otters.

Then there's the brother on the shore. Bede says he's so shaken by what he's seen that he can barely walk home. In the morning he goes to Cuthbert and falls at his feet, in tears, asking forgiveness for spying.
Cuthbert knows already. And he's gentle.

teach.h: TELL NO ONE WHILE I LIVE.
teach.b: He forgives him, on one condition: tell no one what you saw while I'm alive. The brother keeps the promise, and only after Cuthbert's death does the story come out.
So there are two kindnesses in it: animals caring for a man who was cold, and a man caring for a brother who was ashamed.

Cuthbert later lived on Lindisfarne, the island Aidan came to from Iona a few days back on this path. Some readers see in the otters creation at peace with a holy person, like Adam among the animals in Eden.
Others keep it simply as a story of two kindnesses on one cold shore.

how: Christians in the north of England and the Scottish borders honor Saint Cuthbert, and pilgrims visit Lindisfarne, where he lived, and Durham Cathedral, where tradition places his shrine.

games.q: you're the brother who followed Cuthbert. you saw him pray all night in the sea and the animals come to him. now it's morning. what do you do?

say nothing and hope he never knows.
games.why: he falls at Cuthbert's feet and asks forgiveness for spying. Cuthbert forgives him, and asks him to keep it secret while he lives.

practice: Picture an animal that has been gentle with you or with someone you love: a dog leaning against your leg on a bad day, a cat sitting with the one person who's sad, even an animal you once watched caring for its young.
Notice how the kindness was given without words, asking nothing back. If you pray, give thanks for it; if not, let yourself be warmed by the memory.

wordCard.voice: Cuthbert. A monk who stood in prayer in the cold sea at night, and whose feet two otters warmed at dawn, in a secret kept until he died.

carryVoice: Your line: the sea and the otters. Two kindnesses, and a secret kept. Until tomorrow.
